questions.question: Before a trip, you should make sure that:

options.text: The brake pedal sticks.
The gas pedal is loose.
The pedal surfaces are grooved and not worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pedal surfaces are grooved and not worn smooth.
questions.explanation: Check your pedals before driving. Make sure nothing is under or around them that could block movement. The pedals should work properly and have grooved surfaces for grip.

questions.question: If a vehicle carries hazardous cargo, placards must be placed:

options.text: Only on the front of the vehicle.
On the front, rear, and sides of the vehicle.
Only on the driver's side of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, rear, and sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on all four sides of a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo. They must be visible from any direction.

questions.question: When changing lanes, turn signals:

options.text: Should not be used.
Should only be used if a vehicle is close to you.
Should be used every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used every time.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Do not assume other drivers will move out of your way just because you signal.

questions.question: When pulled off on the side of the road:

options.text: A driver should keep the driver's side door open.
A driver should turn on the emergency flashers.
The driver should wave their arms.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver should turn on the emergency flashers.
questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, turn on your four-way emergency flashers. This is very important at night.

questions.question: One way to prevent drowsiness while driving is to:

options.text: Drive alone.
Avoid regular exercise.
Get enough sleep the night before your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get enough sleep the night before your trip.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous. Get a full night's sleep before driving. You can also have someone ride with you, drive during times you are normally awake, and avoid medicines that make you drowsy. Regular exercise helps keep your energy up while driving.

questions.question: What should you do if the brakes cannot build up hydraulic pressure?

options.text: Upshift.
Downshift.
Hold the brake pedal down as far as it will go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshift.
questions.explanation: If your brakes will not build up pressure, try shifting into a lower gear, pumping the brakes, and using the emergency brake.

questions.question: If a train is approaching a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Try to cross the tracks quickly.
Drive around any lowered gates.
Stop and wait for the train to pass before crossing the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the train to pass before crossing the tracks.
questions.explanation: Never try to beat a train across the tracks. It is hard to judge how fast a train is moving. Stop and wait for the train to completely pass before you cross.

questions.question: When checking the fifth wheel gap during a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Make sure the locking jaws are open.
Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: When checking a trailer coupling, make sure the fifth wheel locking jaws are closed tightly around the kingpin shaft.

questions.question: How can you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold the pedal for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release. If the pedal returns to normal position, there may be a problem.
Push the brake pedal down as far as possible and release. If the brake squeaks, there may be a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times, then hold the pedal for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal three times, then press it down hard for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or problem in the brake system.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best advice for driving in fog?

options.text: Try not to drive in fog.
Use your high beam headlights.
Turn off your lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try not to drive in fog.
questions.explanation: Driving in fog is dangerous and should be avoided if possible. If you must drive in fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights, even during the day.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, which action is NOT recommended?

options.text: Move your vehicle to the side of the road
Help injured people
Drive away from the scene

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive away from the scene
questions.explanation: In an accident, you should protect the area, call authorities, help the injured, collect information, and report the accident. Leaving the scene of an accident can result in losing your license.

questions.question: A driver with an open window in cold weather may be:

options.text: A distracted driver
A person dressed too lightly
A person who wants fresh air

questions.correctAnswerText: A distracted driver
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impaired driving. Drivers who are drunk, tired, using drugs, or sick can be dangerous. One warning sign is when a driver rolls down windows in cold weather.

questions.question: Eating while driving:

options.text: Saves time during your trip
Is a good idea on long drives
Takes your attention away from driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes your attention away from driving
questions.explanation: Eating while driving is dangerous. It distracts you from the road and requires you to take at least one hand off the steering wheel.

questions.question: After changing a tire, what should you do?

options.text: Stop shortly after to check that the lug nuts are tight
Repair the brakes
Let air out of the tire to 10 psi

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop shortly after to check that the lug nuts are tight
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short time later to check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: When should you sign a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: After every trip
After any noted defects are fixed
After each time you fill up with fuel

questions.correctAnswerText: After any noted defects are fixed
questions.explanation: Sign a vehicle inspection report only if defects were found and either fixed or marked as not needing repair.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Stay in the vehicle
Get out and call for help
Keep trying to drive off the tracks until you succeed

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and call for help
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave it immediately and move away from the tracks. Find emergency contact information on the signpost and call 911 or the emergency number listed.

questions.question: When turning, when should you turn off the turn signal?

options.text: Before you start the turn
While you are turning
After the turn is finished

questions.correctAnswerText: After the turn is finished
questions.explanation: Keep your turn signal on the whole time you are turning. Do not turn it off until your turn is complete.

questions.question: To stay alert while driving, you should:

options.text: Eat a large meal before you start driving
Keep the cab warm
Drive with another person who can take turns driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with another person who can take turns driving
questions.explanation: Sharing driving duties with another driver reduces fatigue for both drivers. You can also stay alert by avoiding heavy meals and keeping the cab cool.

questions.question: If your brakes fail going downhill, decide what to do quickly because:

options.text: Your vehicle will go faster the longer you wait
More vehicles will have time to move out of your way
Your vehicle will go slower the longer you wait

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle will go faster the longer you wait
questions.explanation: When your brakes fail on a downhill slope, decide quickly what to do. The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go and the harder it will be to stop.

questions.question: To prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop, you should:

options.text: Turn off the engine
Partly engage the clutch
Apply the emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch
questions.explanation: With a manual transmission, partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal. This helps prevent the vehicle from rolling backward when you start moving.
